title: Company All-Hands - November 2025
customer_attendees: Various engineering, product, go-to-market and ops teams
summary: Leadership provided a November update: strong month for hosted usage, progress on Private deployment readiness, a small reorg in Product and Research, and an emphasis on cost/perf optimizations. Roadmap items prioritized: Dedicated autoscaling improvements, KV cache resiliency, and rollout of richer observability. Action items include sharing hiring plan, security docs, and scheduling follow-up deep dives.
action_items: Priya - circulate updated hiring plan and org chart by 2025-11-21
Miguel & Janice - share Dedicated autoscaling RFC and proposed rollout timeline by 2025-11-28
Kevin - publish Q1 roadmap highlights doc and detailedd milestones link to console by 2025-11-20
Dana - update financial runway slide and distribute to managers by 2025-11-18
Rohit - schedule a research deep dive on quantization and model variants (target week of 2025-11-24)
Mark & Alyssa - send a top-10 customer wins one-pager and identify 3 references by 2025-11-25
Security - publish SOC2 artifacts summary and KMS integration notes to internal drive by 2025-11-19
next_steps: Hires and budgeting: managers to submit reqs during next week's planning window
Product teams to post OKR checkpoints in Confluence and link to the roadmap doc
Ops to run a next-week chaos test focused on KV cache failover and share a postmortem
All-hands recording and slides uploaded to drive (link in Slack #all-hands)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (CEO), Miguel Alvarez (CTO), Janice Park (VP Eng), Kevin Brooks (VP Product), Dana Li (COO), Rohit Mehta (Head of Research), Mark Hudson (Head of Sales), Alyssa Chen (Head of CS), plus ~120 remote employees

Summary section (auto): Company momentum update, product highlights, org changes, Q&A.

[00:00] Priya: Good afternoon everyone, welcome to the November all hands, thanks for joining. We've got a pretty full agenda — updates from product, eng, research, go-to-market and then Q&A. We'll try to keep to an hour. Slides are posted in the slack channel, link in the meeting notes.

[00:28] Dana: Quick housekeeping — please put questions in the Q&A panel. We'll try to hit as many as possible and follow up offline where needed. Recording has started.

[00:46] Priya: Alright, high level — revenue and usage. November was a strong month for hosted API usage, up about 18% month-over-month, with a couple of big spikes from trial-to-paid conversions. That helps our unit economics — margins improved as we tuned batching on the runtime. We still need to be careful on costs for peak bursts.

[01:20] Miguel: Yeah, just to add, the runtime optimizations we pushed last sprint — the attention kernel swap — gave about 12% CPU/GPU time reduction for the 70/30 seq length mix we're seeing. There's more in the release notes. We're also seeing cases where the KV cache eviction policy needs to be more resilient; Janice will talk about the autoscaling changes.

[01:55] Janice: Thanks. Quick engineering update: Dedicated autoscale is in internal alpha. The main focus this month is tighter scaling thresholds and better warmup for pools with mixed model families. We're also working on faster fallback to smaller quantized variants if a larger instance saturates. Caveat: there's still edge cases with cold-start latency on some model families.

[02:30] Employee (random): Sorry Janice, do you mean the quantized variants will be automatically chosen?

[02:34] Janice: Yep — policy-based routing will allow preference ordering: latency-first, cost-first, or region-first. We'll have a config UI in the console. Early tests show cost reductions but some variability for rare tokens.

[03:05] Kevin: On product: the roadmap for Q1 has three big bets: 1) Dedicated autoscaling polish and SLA improvements, 2) Private deployment GA for a subset of customers with HSM/KMS workflows, and 3) richer observability — token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing out of the box. We'll publish the detailed milestones later this week.

[03:40] Priya: A couple of org updates: we've consolidated the model onboarding team into Research to speed up variant testing. Rohit will run that group. Also moving two Product Managers into the Private deployment track to accelerate GA. These changes are to reduce handoffs.

[04:05] Rohit: Quick note from Research: quantization experiments are promising — int8 and some mixed-precision paths for newer open models look good. We'll prioritize model-variant evaluations that keep quality within the guardrails for customer workloads. Also planning a public evaluation framework for benchmark reproducibility.

[04:35] Mark: Customer news — three enterprise customers signed renewals this month and one new mid-market customer committed to a Dedicated pilot. We've been using the new benchmark spreadsheet in sales cycles and it's resonating. Kudos to the Solutions team on the PoC templates.

[04:58] Alyssa: From CS — net retention is holding steady, but we're tracking a few renewals that have security questions around VPC and key management. We'll need the security artifacts Miguel mentioned.

[05:20] Miguel: Right. Security update — SOC2 audit is on track, control evidence collection is about 80% complete. We're finalizing the KMS integration tests and will post the summary doc to the drive. Apologies in advance for the slightly messy filenames in the internal folder, team will clean up.

[05:44] Priya: Finance — Dana?

[05:48] Dana: Runway is unchanged from last update, we've extended the budget levers to include more aggressive autoscaling and caching defaults that should reduce infra costs. We'll publish the updated slide with scenarios in the finance folder. We're still tracking towards plan but will be cautious on discretionary spend until the Dedicated revenue curve stabilizes.

[06:18] Employee 2: Any plans to change pricing for embeddings? We saw some customers push back.

[06:25] Mark: We're not changing public pricing this quarter, but we are experimenting with bundling and volume discounts for embeddings in enterprise contracts. We'll share the playbook with AMs.

[06:50] Priya: Ok, let's hit a few product demos and screenshares — Kevin?

[06:54] Kevin: I'll walk through the observability work — I'm going to share the screen, apologies if the pointer lags. (screen share) In the console mock you can see token-level latency heatmaps, per-route cost breakdown, and an anomalies tab that correlates prompt sets with regressions. It's early but the plan is to let teams attach evaluation prompts so regressions trigger alerts.

[07:40] (crosstalk)

[07:45] Janice: On ops note — we're going to start running weekly chaos tests against the KV cache to validate prefix caching fallback paths. Please expect short windows where we intentionally evict keys in staging. This will help reduce P0 incidents in prod.

[08:10] Rohit: One more from research — we observed that some open models have tokenization drift on longer contexts which affects perf. We're building a tokenizer-robustness test into the onboarding pipeline.

[08:40] Priya: Hiring — short summary. We have approvals for 18 hires across eng, research, and sales for Q1. Managers, please post reqs by next Monday so we can prioritize. We're heavier on infra and platform roles right now.

[09:05] Dana: Related to hiring, we're updating our interview loop to include a new exercise for runtime debugging. HR will post the updated hiring doc.

[09:28] (pause, shuffling)

[09:35] Priya: I want to call out customer wins — Mark, can you say more about the Dedicated pilot?

[09:40] Mark: Sure — manufacturer customer signed up for Dedicated because of predictable latency and data isolation. They asked for VPC peering and dedicated KMS — engineering's working through a checklist. The PoC template included a perf spreadsheet; sales used it live in the call which shortened the decision time.

[10:05] Employee 3: Any update on partner integrations with cloud marketplaces?

[10:10] Mark: We're in talks with two cloud marketplaces; timelines are vendor dependent. Marketplace procurement helps some customers who require marketplace billing. We'll share specifics when contracts are finalized.

[10:35] Priya: Alright, questions from the Q&A — first one, SOC2 completion date?

[10:40] Miguel: We're targeting evidence submission by the end of November and final report late December, so 'sock two' is on track. (slight laugh)

[11:05] Q: Can we get more visibility into the Dedicated pricing bands?

[11:10] Dana: We'll publish pricing bands and a calculator in the console. Expect the first version next week; it will be marked experimental.

[11:34] Q: How are we prioritizing Private GA customers?

[11:37] Kevin: Prioritization is based on urgency, security requirements, and willingness to sign an early access agreement. We're targeting a small set for GA to ship a hardened deployable with KMS/HSM options.

[12:05] Priya: A quick note on culture — thanks for the All-Hands feedback form responses. A recurring theme is more async updates; we'll try to regularize product summaries in the #product-updates channel.

[12:30] Janice: Ops note — after the chaos tests we'll run a postmortem and share learnings. Engineers, please opt into the incident rotation if you haven't already.

[12:50] (microphone cough)

[13:00] Rohit: For researchers — internal benchmark framework will land in the repo by end of month. We'll welcome community contributions and reproducible notebooks.

[13:25] Priya: Ok final comments — please review the action items in the notes and reach out if there's anything missing. Big thanks for the hard work — we've shipped a lot this quarter.

[13:40] Dana: Closing logistical note — next all-hands will be in early January after the holiday break. Check the calendar for tentative invites.

[13:55] Priya: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

(Recording ends)
